title: Residual Jump Parity for Epipelagic Correspondence
body_html:
Residual Jump Parity for Epipelagic Correspondence

If two epipelagic representations correspond under theta, then \[ \operatorname{Jump}(B)\subseteq 1/(2m)+(1/m)\mathbb Z. \] Equivalently, one of the two lattice functions has jumps in \((1/m)\mathbb Z\) and the other has jumps in \(1/(2m)+(1/m)\mathbb Z\).
proof_html: The residual moment-map condition gives a nonzero vector in \(B_{-1/(2m)}/B_{-1/(2m)+}\), forcing \(-1/(2m)\) to be a jump of \(B\). The epipelagic jump set restriction epipelagic_theta.epipelagic_jump_set restricts each factor's jump coset to two possibilities, and only the mixed parity case contributes the required tensor jump.
